title: Attack
subtitle: Perform a melee or ranged attack
description: The most common action to take in combat is the Attack action. With this action, you make one melee or ranged attack.

bullets.content: The following rules apply to the Attack action:

items: Certain features, such as Extra Attack, allow you to make more than one attack with this action. You may move between these attacks.
When you attack with a light melee weapon, you can use a bonus action to attack with your other hand (see Two-Weapon Fighting).
You may replace one of your melee attacks with a special attempt to Grapple or a Shove a creature.

bullets.content: Your attack roll may be affected by Advantage or Disadvantage from various conditions.

title: Cast a Spell
subtitle: Use a spell with a 1-action cast time
description: Spellcasters can use their action to cast a spell with a casting time of 1 action.

bullets.content: When casting a spell, keep these rules in mind:

items: You can't cast a spell with your action and another spell with your bonus action in the same turn, unless the action is used to cast a cantrip.
The target must be within the spell's range and not behind total cover.
If a spell requires concentration, you lose concentration if you cast another spell that requires it, become incapacitated, or fail a Constitution saving throw after taking damage.

bullets.content: Material components are not consumed unless the spell's description says otherwise.

title: Dash
subtitle: Gain extra movement
description: When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn equal to your speed, after applying any modifiers.

bullets.content: For example, if your speed is 30 feet, you can move up to 60 feet on your turn if you use the Dash action.

title: Disengage
subtitle: Avoid opportunity attacks
description: If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

bullets.content: This action is useful for safely moving out of an enemy's reach without being attacked.

title: Dodge
subtitle: Focus on avoiding attacks
description: When you take the Dodge action, you focus entirely on avoiding attacks, granting you defensive benefits.

bullets.content: Until the start of your next turn, you gain the following benefits:

items: Any attack roll made against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker.
You make Dexterity saving throws with advantage.

bullets.content: You lose this benefit if you are Incapacitated or if your speed drops to 0.

title: Escape
subtitle: Attempt to escape a grapple
description: A grappled creature can use its action to escape. To do so, it must succeed on a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

bullets.content: Your check is contested by the grappler's Strength (Athletics) check. Escaping other restraints may require a different check, as specified by the effect.

title: Grapple
subtitle: Special melee attack to seize a foe
description: As a special melee attack, you can attempt to grab a creature and subject it to the Grappled condition.

bullets.content: When you want to grab a creature or wrestle with it, you can use the Attack action to make a special melee attack. The following rules apply:

items: The target must be no more than one size larger than you and within your reach.
Using at least one free hand, you make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
If you succeed, the target gains the Grappled condition (its speed becomes 0).

bullets.content: This attempt replaces one of your attacks if you have the Extra Attack feature.

title: Help
subtitle: Aid another creature
description: You can use your action to help another creature, granting it advantage on a check or against an enemy.

bullets.content: You can help in one of two ways:

items: The target gains advantage on the next ability check it makes to perform a task you are helping with.
The target gains advantage on its next attack roll against a creature within 5 feet of you.

bullets.content: The advantage lasts until the start of your next turn.

title: Hide
subtitle: Attempt to become unseen
description: When you take the Hide action, you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check in an attempt to hide.

bullets.content: The following rules apply to hiding:

items: You can't hide from a creature that can see you clearly.
Your check is contested by the Wisdom (Perception) check of any creature actively searching for you.
A creature that isn't searching notices you if your check is lower than its Passive Perception.

bullets.content: If you make noise or are no longer obscured, you give away your position.

title: Improvise
subtitle: Perform an unlisted action
description: You can describe an action not detailed elsewhere. The DM tells you whether it is possible and what kind of roll, if any, you need to make.

bullets.content: This allows for creative problem-solving beyond the standard list of actions.

title: Ready
subtitle: Prepare an action for a trigger
description: You can take the Ready action on your turn, which lets you act using your reaction before the start of your next turn.

bullets.content: To do so, you decide on two things:

items: A perceivable circumstance that will act as a trigger.
The action you will take in response to that trigger (or you can choose to move up to your speed instead).

bullets.content: When the trigger occurs, you can either take your reaction or ignore the trigger.

title: Search
subtitle: Look for something
description: When you take the Search action, you devote your attention to finding something. The DM might require a Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check.

bullets.content: This is useful for finding hidden objects, secret doors, or other details in your environment.

title: Shove
subtitle: Special melee attack to push a foe
description: As a special melee attack, you can shove a creature to knock it prone or push it away from you.

bullets.content: Using the Attack action, you can make a special melee attack to shove a creature. The following rules apply:

items: The target must be no more than one size larger than you and within your reach.
You make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
If you win the contest, you either knock the target prone or push it 5 feet away from you.

bullets.content: This attempt replaces one of your attacks if you have the Extra Attack feature.

title: Stabilize a Creature
subtitle: Aid a dying companion
description: You can use your action to stabilize a creature that has 0 hit points. On a success, the creature is no longer dying.

bullets.content: This requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check. A stable creature regains 1 hit point after 1d4 hours.

title: Use Class Feature
subtitle: Activate a feature requiring an action
description: Many racial traits and class features provide special options for your action.
reference: See class page for more information.

bullets.content: Check your character sheet for any features that specify they require an action to use.

title: Use Object
subtitle: Interact with an object
description: You can interact with one object for free on your turn. If you want to interact with a second object, you must use this action.

bullets.content: This is also the action you take when an object, such as a magical item, requires an action for its use.

title: Use Shield
subtitle: Don or doff a shield
description: A shield takes one action to equip (don) or unequip (doff).

bullets.content: In contrast, armor takes several minutes to don or doff.

title: Climb onto a Bigger Creature*
subtitle: Scale a larger creature
description: A suitably large opponent can be treated as terrain for the purpose of jumping onto its back or clinging to a limb.

bullets.content: The following optional rules apply:

items: The smaller creature uses its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the target's Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
If it wins, the smaller creature moves into the target's space and has advantage on attack rolls against it.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.

title: Disarm*
subtitle: Knock an item from a target's grasp
description: A creature can use a weapon attack to knock a weapon or another item from a target's grasp.

bullets.content: The following optional rules apply:

items: The attacker makes an attack roll contested by the target's Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
If the attacker wins, the attack causes no damage, but the defender drops the item.
The attacker has disadvantage on its attack roll if the target is holding the item with two or more hands.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.

title: Mark*
subtitle: Focus on a target for opportunity attacks
description: This optional rule makes it easier for melee combatants to harry each other with opportunity attacks.

bullets.content: When you make a melee attack, you can also mark your target. The following rules apply:

items: Until the end of your next turn, any opportunity attack you make against the marked target has advantage.
The opportunity attack doesn't expend your reaction, but you can't make the attack if anything is preventing you from taking reactions.
You are limited to one such opportunity attack per turn.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.

title: Overrun*
subtitle: Force movement through a hostile space
description: When a creature tries to move through a hostile creature's space, the mover can try to force its way through by overrunning the hostile creature.

bullets.content: The following optional rules apply:

items: As an action, the mover makes a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the hostile creature's Strength (Athletics) check.
The mover has advantage on this check if it is larger than the hostile creature, or disadvantage if it is smaller.
If the mover wins the contest, it can move through the hostile creature's space once this turn.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.

title: Shove Aside*
subtitle: Push a creature to the side
description: This optional rule allows a creature to use the special shove attack to force a target to an adjacent space.

bullets.content: The following optional rules apply:

items: The attacker has disadvantage on its Strength (Athletics) check when it does so.
If that check is successful, the attacker moves the target 5 feet to a different space within its reach.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.

title: Tumble*
subtitle: Weave through a hostile space
description: A creature can try to tumble through a hostile creature's space, ducking and weaving past the opponent.

bullets.content: The following optional rules apply:

items: As an action, the tumbler makes a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the hostile creature's Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
If the tumbler wins the contest, it can move through the hostile creature's space once this turn.

bullets.content: This is an optional rule from the Dungeon Master's Guide.
